name: Honorius III
description: The pope in 1220, born Cencio Savelli in Rome in the 1140s, elected in 1216; former tutor of Frederick II, determined to reform the Church and recover the Holy Land.

name: Innocent III
description: Predecessor of Honorius III who reformed the Church and called the Fourth Lateran Council in 1213.

name: Frederick II
description: Holy Roman Emperor, tutored by Honorius III and crowned by him in 1220; his delays on crusade hamper recovery of the Holy Land and he is deposed at Lyons in 1245 if history is followed.

name: Gregory IX
description: Cardinal-bishop Ugolino (born 1170), trusted ally of Honorius III famed as papal legate, who succeeds him as pope in 1227 if the saga follows history.

name: Master Willelmus
description: Papal vice-chancellor in 1220, a subdeacon, succeeded in 1222 by Master Guido.

name: Master Guido
description: Papal notary and sub-deacon who becomes vice-chancellor in 1222.

name: Master Fortis
description: One of the papal notaries in 1220, a sub-deacon.

name: Master Obizo
description: One of the papal notaries in 1220, a sub-deacon.

name: Master Maximus
description: One of the papal notaries in 1220, a sub-deacon.

name: Bandinus of Siena
description: Papal corrector in 1220, a deacon.

name: Stefano di Cecanno
description: Cardinal-priest of Saint XII Apostoli (1213), appointed papal camerlengo in 1219.

name: Tommaso da Capua
description: Cardinal-priest of Saint Sabina (1216), appointed penitentiarius in 1219.

name: Peter de Collemdio
description: A papal auditor in 1220.

name: Otto da Tonengo
description: Master Otto, subdeacon and auditor litterarum contradictarum in 1220, succeeded in 1225 by Sinibaldus Fieschi.

name: Sinibaldus Fieschi
description: Master who becomes auditor litterarum contradictarum in 1225 and is elected pope Innocent IV in 1243.

name: Gratian
description: Compiler of the Decretum, a common compendium of papal decrees.

name: Pope Leo IV
description: Pope (847-855) who authored the Homilia Leonis, a popular enumeration of visitation articles.

name: Pope Leo IX
description: Pope who in 1050 controlled no benefices outside the province of Rome.

name: Henri of Toulouse
description: Wealthy merchant in an example petition who, after a holy vision, petitions the papal curia to found a monastery overlooking a river.

name: Count of Toulouse
description: Nobleman whose court supports Henri of Toulouse's petition to found a monastery.

name: Saint Peter
description: The chief apostle, to whom the pope is successor.

name: Jesus Christ
description: From whom the power of the clergy originates through the chain of ordination; the Host is consecrated as his body.

name: Mercury
description: Pagan god whose temple was broken down and rebuilt as a cathedral in a story seed.

name: Pope
description: Head of the Church and bishop of Rome, elected by a two-thirds majority of the cardinals; successor to the apostle Peter.

name: Cardinal
description: Closest advisors of the pope, appointed by him, who aid him in Rome and act as legates; up to 53 at a time in three ranks.

name: Cardinal-bishop
description: Highest rank of cardinal: the bishops of seven small towns near Rome; the pope is ordained by a cardinal-bishop.

name: Cardinal-priest
description: Rank of cardinal; there can be up to 28.

name: Cardinal-deacon
description: Rank of cardinal; there can be up to 18.

name: Bishop
description: Head of a diocese, highest of the major orders; bishops are elected rather than examined and may grant petitions up to Ease Factor 15.

name: Bishop-baron
description: A bishop who is also a feudal lord, typically with about 50 vassal knights, entangled in feudal disputes and warfare against canon law.

name: Archbishop
description: A bishop (metropolitan) with responsibility over up to a dozen neighboring dioceses forming a province; receives the pallium and Commanding Aura.

name: Patriarch
description: Rank between archbishop and pope; the Latin Church has patriarchs at Jerusalem, Antioch, and Constantinople.

name: Primate
description: Rank sought by ambitious archbishops; several archdioceses are raised to primacies in the 13th century, but the effort to create a superior Western rank fails.

name: Archdeacon
description: The bishop's deputy over an archdeaconry; chief judge of canon law there, holding a travelling court and visitation rights; must be a deacon.

name: Dean
description: Either a rural dean heading a deanery of up to two dozen parishes, or the head of a chapter of canons responsible for its discipline.

name: Archpriest
description: Older title used by some rural deans.

name: Vicar-general
description: New diocesan office in a story seed, created by a bishop to hold a canon court visiting rural parishes in place of the archdeacon.

name: Doorkeeper
description: Lowest minor order, held by young boys training for the Church, who receive a pair of keys at ordination.

name: Lector
description: Minor order whose members receive a codex of lessons and now have ceremonial duties.

name: Exorcist
description: Minor order whose members receive a scroll of exorcism rites and gain +1 to exorcisms.

name: Acolyte
description: Greatest of the minor orders, symbolized by an extinguished candlestick and empty vessel; often parish clerks, scribes, or messengers.

name: Sub-deacon
description: Lowest major order; receives paten, chalice, pitcher and basin; serves as parish clerks and canons.

name: Deacon
description: Major order symbolized by a stole over the left shoulder; serves as parish clerk, canon, or archdeacon.

name: Priest
description: Major order ordained by laying on of hands; successors of Christ's 72 disciples; must be freeborn, legitimate, and at least 25.

name: Rector
description: The priest who holds a parish benefice, resides in the parish and holds Mass there.

name: Parish priest
description: Representative of the Church in the parish, reciting the liturgy, distributing alms and caring for his congregation.

name: Parish clerk
description: Assistant to the parish priest (often an acolyte) who helps with the liturgy and rings bells, paid a yearly wage by parishioners.

name: Curate
description: Priest who performs the liturgical duties of an absent parish priest for a fraction of the benefice.

name: Chaplain
description: Priest appointed to hold Mass in a chapel.

name: Co-adjudicator
description: Priest appointed by the bishop to perform the duties of an ill, senile, or mad parish priest.

name: Proctor
description: Representative of bishops, nobles, or religious houses at the papal curia who presents and appeals petitions.

name: Papal legate
description: Representative of the pope, appointed in several grades; legates may have been sent to investigate Hermetic covenants and Tribunals.

name: Legati a latere
description: Highest grade of papal legate, usually cardinals, with the widest powers including decisions binding even the pope.

name: Legati missi
description: Grade of papal legate (nuncio) given a particular mission, often priests or deacons from the capellani.

name: Legati nati
description: Historic title held by some archbishops (vicarii apostolici) that by 1220 carries no real power.

name: Vice-Chancellor
description: Head of the papal chancery since the office of chancellor was suppressed in 1216.

name: Notary
description: Official who records and standardizes petitions; six serve in the papal chancery, and canon judges employ one.

name: Abbreviatores
description: Assistants to the papal notaries, two or three each.

name: Corrector
description: Chancery official who approves drafted papal letters; usually two.

name: Bullatores
description: Chancery officials who hold the papal seal.

name: Data communis
description: Public reading of petitions performed by the vice-chancellor and notaries.

name: Camerlengo
description: Director of the papal camera (finances).

name: Collector
description: Papal financial officials under the camerlengo.

name: Thesaurarius
description: Administrator of the papal treasure; also an assistant to a chapter's custos.

name: Penitentiarius
description: Cardinal who deals with appeals to penances, grants dispensations and is confessor to the cardinals, with up to 12 sub-penitentiarii.

name: Auditores
description: Temporary papal judges appointed case by case who may judge any case or petition brought to the papacy.

name: Auditor litterarum contradictarum
description: Papal official who receives appeals to petitions and arbitrates compromises.

name: Summoner
description: Official (apparitor) who summons people to canon court, charging fees; prone to corruption.

name: Canon
description: Member of a chapter of clergy serving an urban church who share common table and property.

name: Canoness
description: Members of chapters of canonesses in parts of France, Germany and northern Italy, subservient to a chapter of canons.

name: Provost
description: Historic head of a chapter of canons, assisted by the camerarius and cellerarius; largely disappeared by 1220.

name: Cantor
description: Chapter office responsible for organizing the liturgy and sacred rites.

name: Scholasticus
description: Chapter office (or chancellor) responsible for the church school.

name: Custos
description: Chapter office responsible for the church treasury, assisted by thesaurarius and sacrista.

name: Hebdomadarius
description: The canon whose weekly turn it is to lead the liturgy.

name: Anchorite
description: Male (or anchoress, female) recluse living in a cell in a church devoted to worship.

name: Energumen
description: A victim possessed by a demon.

name: Catechumen
description: Adults undergoing instruction in Christianity prior to baptism.

name: Peregrinator
description: Itinerant magus.

name: Quaesitor
description: Hermetic investigator; a player magus may be made a Quaesitor to act as proctor for the Order at the curia.

name: Magus
description: Hermetic wizard; magi attend councils, owe tithes and may be excommunicated.

name: Covenfolk
description: Mundane inhabitants of a covenant who worship at chapels and may be baptized.

name: The Church
description: The Ecclesiastical hierarchy of Mythic Europe, a bureaucracy whose resources characters may mobilize via petitions.

name: Papal Curia
description: The papal court, enlarged and streamlined under Innocent III and Honorius III; receives up to 2,000 petitions yearly and is the final court of appeal.

name: Papal Chancery
description: Office of the curia controlling correspondence between the pope and Christendom.

name: Papal Camera
description: Office of the curia controlling papal finances, directed by the camerlengo.

name: Penitentiaria
description: Papal judicial office handling lesser petitions, penances and dispensations.

name: Capellani
description: The college of priests, deacons and sub-deacons serving in Rome; 70 in 1220.

name: Order of Hermes
description: The order of magi; the papacy is in some sense aware of it and may send legates to its covenants and Tribunals.

name: Chapter of Canons
description: Community of clergy serving an urban church who share common table and property; ranges from six to a few dozen canons.

name: Augustinian Canons
description: Regular canons following the Rule of Saint Augustine.

name: Secular Canons
description: More lax chapters of canons who may eat meat, wear linen and own property.

name: Military Orders
description: Orders of knights whose heads attended Lateran IV; a church may be an outpost of one.

name: Latin Church
description: The Western Church, which has appointed patriarchs at Jerusalem, Antioch, and Constantinople.

name: Greek Church
description: The Eastern Church, which participated little in Lateran IV and is temporarily reunited in 1274.

name: Benedictines
description: Monks of a Benedictine monastery in Italy who agree to colonize Henri of Toulouse's new monastery.

name: Saracens
description: Enemies against whom the 1245 council calls a crusade.

name: Mongols
description: Invaders against whom the 1245 council calls a crusade; can cause a diocese to be in partibus infidelium.

name: Papal States
description: Italian territories of the papacy that rebelled against Honorius III.

name: Diocese
description: Territorial jurisdiction of a bishop, containing several hundred to a thousand parishes.

name: In partibus infidelium
description: Status of a diocese overrun by infidels or lost to catastrophe, whose bishop lives outside it.

name: Province
description: An archbishop's jurisdiction over neighboring dioceses.

name: Fila specialis
description: Dioceses directly subject to Rome rather than to a province.

name: Archdeaconry
description: Territorial subset of a diocese under an archdeacon.

name: Deanery
description: Group of up to two dozen rural parishes under a rural dean.

name: Parish
description: Main unit of Ecclesiastic administration, centered on a parish church.

name: Minster
description: Older superior church with aristocratic patronage ruling subordinate churches; some persist in 1220.

name: Parish church
description: Church at the center of parish life, consecrated by the bishop with relics under its altar; base Divine aura 4.

name: Cathedral
description: The church of the bishop, usually the largest in the diocese's main town.

name: Chapel
description: Subordinate church with a chaplain, usually without bells, font or cemetery; Divine aura 3.

name: Private chapel
description: Chapel of nobles, castles, or guilds licensed for private use.

name: Church Auras
description: Divine auras radiating from a church altar as far as the bells can be heard, levels 1 to 5.

name: Commanding Aura
description: Supernatural power of senior Church officials, received by archbishops, which a magus can resist.

name: Pallium
description: Archbishop's symbol of office, received from the pope or a papal legate.

name: Canon law
description: Law of the Church based on papal decrees, claiming jurisdiction over religious obligations and moral offenses.

name: Canon court
description: Church courts held by archdeacons, bishops, and the curia, with no jury and no power to shed blood.

name: Compurgation
description: Canon court ritual in which about a dozen witnesses swear to the defendant's good character, acquitting him.

name: Excommunication
description: Punishment for repeat serious offenses denying benefit of Sacraments except penance and burial in consecrated ground.

name: Irregularity
description: Divine punishment of clergy who commit grossly immoral crimes, preventing use of Faith Points until confession.

name: Monition
description: Official warning, usually for first-time offenders.

name: Public penance
description: Canon punishment such as clergy chanting the psalter at each other or providing rushes for the church floor.

name: Interdict
description: Church sanction on a town or kingdom obtainable by petition.

name: Shedding of Blood
description: Clerics are forbidden to shed blood or be involved in blood punishments, reiterated at Lateran IV.

name: Simony
description: Buying and selling of sacred things, a canon law crime.

name: Usury
description: Charging excessive interest, both a canon and secular crime.

name: Sanctuary
description: The church, churchyard and cemetery are places where fugitives may shelter for up to 40 days.

name: Slander
description: A canon offense since 1215.

name: Sorcery
description: Minor sorcery occasionally tried in canon courts; serious cases by secular courts.

name: Heresy
description: Heretical belief, prompting more frequent visitation; magi's views are likely heretical to the Church.

name: Tithe
description: Tenth of income paid to the Church; Hermetic covenants are not exempt.

name: Benefice
description: Income associated with a parish church, assigned to a priest.

name: Pluralism
description: Practice of a single priest holding several benefices, technically outlawed.

name: Glebe
description: Plot of land forming part of a rural benefice farmed by the priest.

name: Servitia communia
description: A third of yearly income paid to the papacy by a newly appointed bishop or abbot.

name: Perambulation
description: Procession on Rogation Day in which priest and parishioners walk the parish boundary.

name: Rogation Day
description: April 25th, the day of the perambulation.

name: Visitation
description: Annual inspection of parishes by the bishop or his deputies, using a checklist of about 100 articles.

name: Visitatio ad Limina
description: Canon law requirement that bishops report in person to the pope every four years.

name: Synod
description: Meeting of clergy convoked by deans, archdeacons, bishops or archbishops.

name: Ecumenical Council
description: Special synod called and presided over by the pope; twelve have been held.

name: Fourth Lateran Council
description: Ecumenical council of 1215 called by Innocent III, reiterating the ban on clerics shedding blood and ordering visitation of heretic parishes.

name: Third Lateran Council
description: Council of 1179 that set limits on the retinues of senior clergy.

name: Council of Lyons
description: Ecumenical councils held at Lyons in 1245 (deposing Frederick II) and 1274 (temporary reunion with the Greek Church).

name: Crusade
description: Holy war; papal taxes are levied for crusades and calling one requires a petition Ease Factor 42.

name: Minor Orders
description: Clerical grades of doorkeeper, lector, exorcist and acolyte, who may marry.

name: Major Orders
description: Clerical grades of sub-deacon, deacon, priest and bishop, who are celibate.

name: Ordination
description: Ceremony marking each step through the orders, requiring an oral examination; also a Sacrament conducted by a bishop.

name: Ordination Examination Total
description: Intelligence + Church Lore or Civil and Canon Law + stress die compared to an Ease Factor per rank.

name: Rapid Ordination
description: Acceleration through several grades at once, granting only 1 Faith Point.

name: Dispensation
description: Exception granted by bishop or pope, e.g. for priests not meeting ordination criteria.

name: Tonsure
description: Shaved head worn by all clerical orders.

name: Sacraments
description: Seven supernatural Divine powers conducted by priests that need not Penetrate but require willing participants.

name: Baptism
description: Sacrament granting a baptismal name; performed by a priest it dispels non-Divine nonpermanent supernatural effects.

name: Baptismal name
description: Name received at baptism that cannot be used as a Sympathetic Connection.

name: Confirmation
description: Sacrament conducted only by a bishop, granting a Faith Point.

name: Mass
description: Most sacred Sacrament (Eucharist, Holy Communion) turning bread and wine into the body and blood of Christ.

name: Marriage
description: Sacrament granting husband and wife a Faith Point.

name: Penance
description: Sacrament absolving confessed sins through a penance task, granting a special Confidence Point.

name: Extreme Unction
description: Last Rites absolving mortal sins; the body cannot be affected by other supernatural powers for three days.

name: Liturgy
description: The church service in Latin, with the priest facing east before the altar.

name: Host
description: Bread consecrated as the body of Christ.

name: Faith Points
description: Points gained from Sacraments and ordination, usable like Confidence Points.

name: Confidence Points
description: Points spent to add +3 to totals such as the Exorcism Total.

name: Possession
description: Demonic control of a victim by investing Infernal Might.

name: Exorcism
description: Divine supernatural power to expel a possessing demon; Exorcism Total = stress die + bonuses vs Might invested.

name: Relics
description: Remains or objects of saints with a Faith Score granting Magic Resistance and an aura hostile to the Infernal.

name: Faith Score
description: Rating of a relic determining its Faith Points and Divine Might.

name: Magic Resistance
description: Resistance that exorcism must Penetrate; granted by holding a relic.

name: Penetration
description: Requirement for supernatural effects to overcome Magic Resistance.

name: Might
description: Supernatural power score of creatures; Divine and Infernal Might.

name: Aura
description: Supernatural aura that affects totals; church auras are Divine.

name: Regio
description: Supernatural region; covenants hidden in one need not pay tithe.

name: Petitioning the Church
description: Rules for convincing the Church to act, generating a Petition Total vs an Ease Factor.

name: Petition Total
description: Com (written) or Pre (audience) + Church Lore + modifiers, with no die roll.

name: Appealing a Petition
description: Overturning another's petition requires original Petition Total + 3.

name: Argument Success
description: Int + Ability + stress die vs 9 to gain petition modifiers.

name: Reputation
description: Characters gain or lose Church Lore or Civil and Canon Law reputation from ordination exams; affects petitions.

name: Social Status
description: Gained appropriately on ordination.

name: The Gift
description: Supernatural gift of magi causing social penalties, applied to audience petitions.

name: Wizard War
description: Hermetic sanctioned conflict between magi.

name: Interference in the mundane
description: Hermetic crime a magus may be prosecuted for.

name: Covenant
description: Home of magi; may hold benefices, chapels, and owe tithes.

name: Tribunal
description: Hermetic regional meeting that papal legates may have investigated.

name: Vis
description: Magical raw power; churches may control vis sources, usually Divine-tainted.

name: Enchanted Items
description: Magic items churches may possess, costing 1 Build Point per level.

name: Build Points
description: Points used to purchase church resources as for covenants.

name: Hooks
description: Story elements for churches that provide points for Boons.

name: Boons
description: Advantages for churches or covenants bought with Hook points.

name: Specialists
description: Characters serving the Church in limited ways, bought with Build Points.

name: Typical Source of Income
description: Income level granted by some Boons.

name: Archdeacon Agent
description: Major Covenant Boon: the local archdeacon is an agent of the covenant.

name: Holder of Benefices
description: Minor Covenant Boon: the covenant holds parish benefices.

name: Covenant Chapel
description: Covenant Boon: a private chapel with a Divine aura of 3 at the covenant; +20 to Loyalty.

name: Military Order (Church Boon)
description: Major Church Boon: the church is an outpost of a military order.

name: Anchorite (Church Boon)
description: Minor Church Boon: an anchorite's cell raising the Divine aura by 1.

name: Burial Rights
description: Minor Church Boon: large cemetery collecting burial fees.

name: Chantry
description: Minor Church Boon: income from reciting Masses for the dead.

name: Chapter of Canons (Church Boon)
description: Minor Church Boon: the priests form a chapter holding benefices.

name: Church School
description: Minor Church Boon: a school attached to the church.

name: Corrupt
description: Major Church Hook: corrupt priests give the church an Infernal aura.

name: Heretics
description: Major Church Hook: priests with heretical beliefs.

name: Jurisdiction
description: Major Church Hook: the church has jurisdiction over many subordinate churches.

name: Rule of Saint Augustine
description: Monk-like rule followed by regular canons.

name: Longevity potion
description: Magus potion that may sterilize, technically a canon offense.

name: Boundary target
description: Spell target that can affect a well-defined parish or diocese.

name: Structure target
description: Target that can affect an entire church; nave and tower floors count as Rooms.

name: Sympathetic Connection
description: Link aiding Penetration, which a baptismal name cannot provide.

name: Ordeals
description: Trials clerics may not be involved in.

name: Proctor of Hermes
description: Story seed position: a magus Quaesitor representing the Order at the papal curia.

name: License of Absence
description: Minor Virtue allowing a priest with a benefice to be absent.

name: Gentle Gift
description: Virtue ideal for a magus acting as proctor for the Order.

name: Divine
description: Realm of God; Sacraments, exorcism and church auras are Divine.

name: Infernal
description: Realm of demons; relics are hostile to it and corrupt churches have Infernal auras.

name: Magic
description: Magic Realm, reachable via a temple gateway in a story seed.

name: The Great Discord
description: CrVi 55 Ritual that taints a parish so everyone suffers The Gift's social penalties for a Moon.

name: Decretum
description: Gratian's compendium of papal decrees; Civil and Canon Law Summa Level 5 Quality 11.

name: Homilia Leonis
description: Church Lore Tractatus Quality 8 by Pope Leo IV listing visitation articles.

name: The Bible
description: Summa of Theology Level 10 Quality 3 and Church Lore Level 3.

name: Parish Register
description: Summa of Area Lore of the parish, Quality 5.

name: Missal
description: Tractatus in Church Lore and Music with the text for Mass; every church has one.

name: Breviary
description: Church Lore Tractatus with prayers for canonical hours.

name: Codex of lessons
description: Church Lore Tractatus received by lectors at ordination.

name: Scroll of exorcism rites
description: Received by exorcists at ordination.

name: Holy water
description: Adds +1 to exorcism.

name: Crucifix
description: Adds +1 to exorcism.

name: Stole
description: Symbol of deacon and priest office.

name: Paten
description: Plate for bread given to sub-deacons with a chalice.

name: Papal seal
description: Held by the bullatores.

name: Baptismal font
description: Font in parish churches; baptism there grants a Faith Point.

name: Church Lore
description: Knowledge of liturgies used in ordination and petitions.

name: Civil and Canon Law
description: Knowledge of canon used for ordination and petition arguments.

name: Artes Liberales
description: Includes Logic for petition arguments.

name: Intrigue
description: Ability for petition arguments.

name: Area Lore
description: Ability gained through visitation.

name: Ride
description: Ability gained through visitation.

name: Theology
description: Subject of church libraries and the Bible.

name: Music
description: Subject of the missal.

name: Latin
description: Needed to read exorcism rites.

name: Creo
description: Technique of The Great Discord.

name: Vim
description: Form of The Great Discord.

name: Rego
description: Technique used with Mentem to sway clergy.

name: Mentem
description: Form used to sway clergy.

name: Intellego
description: Technique for scrying as magical evidence.

name: Intelligence
description: Characteristic used in ordination and argument rolls.

name: Communication
description: Characteristic for written petitions.

name: Presence
description: Characteristic for audience petitions.

name: Rome
description: Seat of the pope; rebelled against Honorius III.

name: Mythic Europe
description: The setting.

name: Holy Land
description: Goal of crusade recovery.

name: Ostia
description: Cardinal-bishop town near Rome.

name: Porto
description: Cardinal-bishop town.

name: Silva Candida
description: Cardinal-bishop town.

name: Albano
description: Cardinal-bishop town.

name: Sabina
description: Cardinal-bishop town.

name: Tusculum
description: Cardinal-bishop town.

name: Palestrina
description: Cardinal-bishop town.

name: Saint XII Apostoli
description: Titular church of Stefano di Cecanno.

name: Saint Sabina
description: Titular church of Tommaso da Capua.

name: Scotland
description: Mostly fila specialis dioceses.

name: Leon
description: Diocese subject to Rome.

name: Cartagena
description: Diocese subject to Rome.

name: Burgos
description: Diocese subject to Rome.

name: Bamberg
description: Diocese subject to Rome.

name: Pavia
description: Diocese subject to Rome.

name: Ferrara
description: Diocese subject to Rome.

name: Jerusalem
description: Latin patriarchate.

name: Antioch
description: Latin patriarchate.

name: Constantinople
description: Latin patriarchate and council site.

name: Mainz
description: Archdiocese raised to primacy; 22 archdeacons.

name: Cologne
description: Archdiocese; four archdeacons.

name: Trier
description: Archdiocese raised to primacy.

name: Magdeburg
description: Archdiocese raised to primacy.

name: Salzburg
description: Archdiocese raised to primacy.

name: Saint Andrew's
description: Scottish archdiocese raised to primacy.

name: Armagh
description: Irish archdiocese.

name: Lund
description: Scandinavian archdiocese.

name: Gniezno
description: Polish archdiocese.

name: Toledo
description: Spanish archdiocese.

name: Tarragona
description: Spanish archdiocese.

name: Esztergom
description: Hungarian archdiocese.

name: Canterbury
description: Diocese with one archdeacon.

name: Constance
description: Ten archdeacons.

name: Munster
description: 34 archdeacons.

name: Hildesheim
description: 40 archdeacons.

name: London
description: City with over 100 parishes.

name: Paris
description: City with over 100 parishes.

name: Florence
description: City with over 100 parishes.

name: Lyons
description: Site of councils 1245 and 1274.

name: Long Melford
description: Parish petitioning to move feast days in 1220.

name: Toulouse
description: Home of Henri of Toulouse.

name: Siena
description: Home of Bandinus.

name: Nicaea
description: Site of councils 325 and 787.

name: Ephesus
description: Council 431.

name: Chalcedon
description: Council 451.

name: Temple of Mercury
description: Roman temple rebuilt as a cathedral, potentially a regio gateway.

name: Germany
description: Region with bishop-barons.

name: Spain
description: Region with bishop-barons.

name: France
description: Region.

name: England
description: Region.

name: Italy
description: Region.

description: Region.

description: Region.
